summary: This Sporting News guide explains line shopping, the practice of comparing odds and lines for the same bet across multiple online sportsbooks to get better prices. It covers how sportsbooks set and move lines, how to shop efficiently with live odds feeds or multiple apps, and why futures markets offer especially large differences. It stresses that line shopping doesn't pick more winners but improves chances, increases wins and reduces losses.
one_line: A guide to line shopping, comparing odds across online sportsbooks to get better lines, bigger wins and cheaper losses.
key_facts: Line shopping means checking lines and odds for a prospective bet at multiple online sportsbooks, which often yields better odds and improved lines.
The best sportsbooks employ oddsmakers and oddsmaking services; other betting apps simply copy those lines.
Oddsmakers use computer models and algorithms considering analytics, statistics, injury and roster news, performance and matchup data.
Sportsbooks aim to even out betting on both sides so they earn the profit built into the odds regardless of which side wins.
Betting differs between sportsbooks, so one book may move a line because of betting while another doesn't, creating line differences.
Caesars' point spreads can be a half-point to two points better than the competition's, and its moneyline odds may be more favorable.
DraftKings has more open betting markets than most online sportsbooks, and FanDuel and BetMGM run many promos and odds boosts.
Odds in futures markets can vary significantly between sportsbooks, since books sometimes have higher liabilities on specific teams and offer better odds on others to lay that off.
Once you bet, you lock in the odds or line as posted; later changes, better or worse, don't affect your bet.
Example: if three of four sportsbooks have the Chiefs at -3 against the Bengals but the fourth has -2.5, a three-point Chiefs win pushes at three books but wins at the fourth.
Las Vegas sportsbooks set the standard, and most online sites use the Vegas line as a foundation for setting lines in every major sport.
Lines that move for legitimate reasons like an injury move at every sportsbook, but lines that move due to betting patterns change only at the book that saw the betting, which is the opportunity.
